plugin.description: Thirty-nine independently usable agent skills for project writing, product narrative, developer adoption, commercial research and consistent project meaning.
plugin.short_description: Writing, product narrative and developer growth
plugin.long_description: Choose a focused skill for the work at hand: shape product positioning and story, write a compelling GitHub README, improve developer adoption, refine prose, or continue Geekist's project writing, architecture and research practices. Upstream skills are preserved with attribution and can be installed individually. There is no required sequence.
default_prompts: Make this GitHub README more compelling while staying faithful to the product.
Position this product for the developers who will benefit from it.
Improve this writing while preserving its meaning and voice.
Research this company for credible collaboration or paid-work opportunities.

advance-with-uncertainty.title: Advance through evidence gaps
advance-with-uncertainty.purpose: Describe evidence gaps accurately and connect them to useful next actions.
advance-with-uncertainty.when_to_use: Use when an unrun check or uncertain claim is preventing independent authorised work.
advance-with-uncertainty.example_request: Turn this untested adapter decision into bounded next actions and clear completion evidence.
advance-with-uncertainty.expected_result: A precise gap, the next check, the dependent step and the work that can continue.

example.before: Compatibility is unproven. Stop implementation.
example.after: Implement the authorised adapter. Check one local client event before claiming compatibility; the check is still pending.
example.source_facts: The adapter implementation is authorised. Compatibility has not been checked. One local client-event check is required before claiming compatibility.

advance-with-uncertainty.source_basis: This skill implements the Geekist requirement to make evidence gaps actionable. Related decision principles draw on MADR. It helps agents describe what remains unresolved while identifying useful next actions, without treating ordinary pending work as a reason to abandon an authorised implementation.
advance-with-uncertainty.activation_description: Turn evidence gaps and unresolved questions into bounded next actions while preserving honest claims and actual blockers. Use when drafting or reviewing tasks, ADRs, plans, assessments or worker handoffs, especially when labels such as unproven, unqualified or no evidence are being used to reject options or halt authorised implementation.

interface.short_description: Turn evidence gaps into bounded next actions
interface.default_prompt: Use $advance-with-uncertainty to record this evidence gap and continue the authorised work with clear validation and blocker criteria.

backend-slice-architecture.title: Review backend ownership and boundaries
backend-slice-architecture.purpose: Apply capability-first organisation with explicit orchestration and protected public boundaries.
backend-slice-architecture.when_to_use: Use when designing or reviewing a backend against this chosen model.
backend-slice-architecture.example_request: Review this service boundary using the existing backend rules; preserve local naming and propose the smallest migration.
backend-slice-architecture.expected_result: A boundary recommendation tied to the existing rules, code and concrete consequences.

example.before: Put the checkout and stock workflows into a shared helper.
example.after: Keep checkout and stock rules inside their capabilities. Coordinate the cross-capability workflow in the existing application surface.
example.source_facts: Checkout and stock are separate owned capabilities. A workflow coordinates both through the existing application surface.

backend-slice-architecture.source_basis: The backend playbook expresses [@pipewrk](https://github.com/pipewrk)'s capability-first architecture rules. Editorial guidance improves the presentation while retaining the public boundaries and orchestration requirements established by the architecture.
backend-slice-architecture.activation_description: Use when creating, refactoring, reviewing, or incrementally migrating backend architecture towards a capability-first, package-shaped model with explicit public APIs, clear orchestration, and earned shared infrastructure across apps, packages, libraries, modules, or equivalent project roots.

interface.default_prompt: Use $backend-slice-architecture to review backend placement, public boundaries, orchestration, and incremental migration.

establish-project-language.title: Establish shared project terminology
establish-project-language.purpose: Establish agreed meanings for project concepts before contributing agents develop incompatible vocabularies.
establish-project-language.when_to_use: Use when onboarding to a domain, reconciling competing terms or introducing a consequential concept.
establish-project-language.example_request: Find what eligible means in this project and reconcile the code, decisions and interface wording.
establish-project-language.expected_result: A sourced terminology record with context, accepted meanings, aliases and unresolved differences.

example.before: Ready, approved and eligible all mean the account can proceed.
example.after: Keep the three labels distinct until sources establish their meanings. Record which condition permits the account to proceed.
example.source_facts: The sources use ready, approved and eligible. Their equivalence has not been established, and each may express a different condition.

establish-project-language.source_basis: This skill draws on DDD bounded contexts and SKOS concept distinctions, together with terminology practices from Good Docs. It helps contributors agree on the meanings used within a project so that subsequent documents can refer to the same concepts consistently.
establish-project-language.activation_description: Discover, reconcile and maintain project concepts and terminology from code, schemas, tests, decisions and existing content. Use when starting a project, onboarding to an existing domain, resolving competing meanings, proposing new terms, or establishing shared language across agents and artefacts.

interface.short_description: Establish shared project terms and meanings
interface.default_prompt: Use $establish-project-language to establish the concepts and vocabulary in this repository.

frontend-slice-architecture.title: Review frontend features and scenes
frontend-slice-architecture.purpose: Organise frontend features around clear ownership and appropriate shared components.
frontend-slice-architecture.when_to_use: Use when designing or reviewing a frontend against this chosen model.
frontend-slice-architecture.example_request: Review these feature and scene boundaries without changing the framework or underlying frontend rules.
frontend-slice-architecture.expected_result: A targeted recommendation preserving feature ownership, public surfaces and scene composition.

example.before: The shared button should own the checkout workflow state.
example.after: Keep checkout workflow state in its feature. Let the scene compose the feature with shared UI primitives.
example.source_facts: Checkout owns its workflow state. The shared button is a UI primitive, and scenes compose features.

frontend-slice-architecture.source_basis: The frontend playbook expresses [@pipewrk](https://github.com/pipewrk)'s feature-first architecture rules. Its guidance clarifies ownership and shared-component boundaries without changing the underlying engineering decisions.
frontend-slice-architecture.activation_description: Use when creating, refactoring, reviewing, or incrementally migrating frontend architecture towards a feature-first, package-shaped model with explicit public APIs, thin scene-level composition, and earned shared UI and hooks.

interface.short_description: Review feature ownership and scene composition
interface.default_prompt: Use $frontend-slice-architecture to review frontend placement, public boundaries, scene composition, and incremental migration.

record-architecture-decisions.title: Record clear architecture decisions
record-architecture-decisions.purpose: Document the reasoning behind technical decisions while that reasoning is still available to the people who made them.
record-architecture-decisions.when_to_use: Use for a formal decision record or a clear explanation of why a technical choice was made.
record-architecture-decisions.example_request: Record why we chose a shared queue, including alternatives, the pending latency check and when to reconsider.
record-architecture-decisions.expected_result: A decision record with context, options, outcome, consequences and explicit evidence status.

example.before: The shared queue is the best option and will meet the latency target.
example.after: Choose the shared queue for this prototype. Measure latency before claiming the target is met; record what result would trigger reconsideration.
example.source_facts: The shared queue is chosen for a prototype. Latency has not been measured, so meeting the target is still a pending claim.

record-architecture-decisions.source_basis: MADR informs the decision structure, while source checks preserve the status and authority of the decision. The guidance helps maintainers understand why an approach was selected, particularly after the original participants have moved on and the meeting that settled the matter has become a distant organisational legend.
record-architecture-decisions.activation_description: Write, explain, revise or summarise the rationale for a consequential technical decision, formally as an ADR or informally for future readers. Use for accepted choices, alternatives, trade-offs, decision drivers, consequences and reconsideration conditions. Not for general architecture design or technical research without a decision.

review-project-language.title: Review clarity and consistent meaning
review-project-language.purpose: Improve writing while checking its consistency with established terminology and source material.
review-project-language.when_to_use: Use when existing prose needs editing, rewriting, polishing or review, including drafts, READMEs, reports, messages and research findings. It can also provide a finishing pass after another writing skill.
review-project-language.example_request: Review this task, decision and announcement for consistent meanings and explain every consequential edit.
review-project-language.expected_result: Located findings or an authorised revision that preserves meanings, constraints and source claims.

example.before: Improve the eligibility coverage signal across the activation surface.
example.after: Explain what eligibility and coverage mean here, then name the behaviour that should change. Keep eligibility and coverage distinct.
example.source_facts: Eligibility and coverage are distinct project concepts. Their definitions and the intended behaviour need to be established before rewriting the requirement.

review-project-language.source_basis: This skill combines document-first editing with source-integrity checks. It also provides for inspectable revisions where the consequences of an editorial change warrant explanation. Deliberate authorial voice is preserved rather than automatically normalised.
review-project-language.activation_description: Review, edit, rewrite or polish existing prose for clarity, flow, faithful meaning, consistent terminology, voice and accessible navigation. Use when a draft, README, report, research finding, message or other writing needs improvement, including a finishing pass after another writing skill.

interface.short_description: Review clarity, claims and consistent meaning

write-implementation-tasks.title: Write actionable implementation tasks
write-implementation-tasks.purpose: Express implementation work through clear objectives and acceptance criteria, with the relevant constraints preserved.
write-implementation-tasks.when_to_use: Use when outcomes, behaviour, validation, dependencies or ownership need to be expressed clearly in a task, acceptance criteria, handoff or plan.
write-implementation-tasks.example_request: Write a task for members to export their own bookings; keep the access restriction and include failure cases.
write-implementation-tasks.expected_result: A task with observable behaviour, acceptance criteria, validation and precise dependencies.

example.before: Improve export support and validate permissions.
example.after: Let members export their own bookings. Reject exports of another member’s bookings and verify both outcomes.
example.source_facts: Members may export their own bookings. They may not export another member’s bookings.

write-implementation-tasks.source_basis: Goal-oriented task structure is combined with source-preserving editing practices informed by Humanizer and Plain Writing. The skill helps agents describe work in terms an engineer can act upon, while retaining the constraints that determine whether the result is acceptable.
write-implementation-tasks.activation_description: Write or refine actionable work, including implementation tasks, tickets, acceptance criteria, worker handoffs, follow-up actions and execution plans. Use when outcomes, behaviour, validation, dependencies or ownership need to be expressed clearly.

write-interface-content.title: Write interface copy for real states
write-interface-content.purpose: Explain application behaviour so users understand what happened and how to proceed.
write-interface-content.when_to_use: Use for labels, errors, empty states, progress messages and dashboard wording.
write-interface-content.example_request: Write the interrupted-export message using the actual state contract; do not imply the download completed.
write-interface-content.expected_result: State-accurate interface wording, consistent action names and useful recovery.

example.before: Export success: processing incomplete.
example.after: Your export stopped before completion. Try again.
example.source_facts: The export stopped before completion. The product supports trying again.

write-interface-content.source_basis: The guidance draws on Atlassian's state-aware content practices. It encourages wording that reflects application behaviour and provides useful recovery information, especially where a generic error message would leave the user wondering what the application expects them to do.
write-interface-content.activation_description: Write or revise UX and in-product language: button labels, forms, dashboards, status and progress messages, errors, empty states, tooltips, onboarding and notifications. Use when wording must reflect actual product behaviour and help people act. Use marketing content for campaigns and public positioning.

interface.short_description: Write clear copy for actual product states

write-marketing-content.title: Explain supported product value
write-marketing-content.purpose: Communicate product value through credible claims and an appropriate editorial voice.
write-marketing-content.when_to_use: Use for audience-facing product communication, including product descriptions, README introductions, landing pages, positioning, portfolio narratives, launches, newsletters and social posts. Interface content remains a separate specialist when needed.
write-marketing-content.example_request: Announce booking exports for members; preserve that background scheduling has not shipped.
write-marketing-content.expected_result: Customer-facing value grounded in actual behaviour, with stronger claims separated for validation.

example.before: Automatically export all your bookings every day.
example.after: Download your bookings when you need them.
example.source_facts: Members can download bookings on demand. Automatic daily scheduling has not shipped.

write-marketing-content.source_basis: This skill connects audience needs to supported product value, incorporating factual checks and voice-sensitive editing informed by Humanizer and Plain Language Editor. The resulting copy should be engaging while remaining accountable to actual product behaviour.
write-marketing-content.activation_description: Write or refine audience-facing product communication, including product descriptions, README introductions, landing pages, positioning, portfolio narratives, launch announcements, newsletters and social posts. Use when explaining a product to its audience, whether or not a call to action is specified; use interface content for in-product states and controls.

interface.short_description: Explain product value with supported claims

write-project-content.title: Write General Project Content
write-project-content.purpose: Write and revise general project prose without imposing a document template.
write-project-content.when_to_use: Use whenever a request needs substantive project prose, including research notes, reports, findings, summaries, progress updates and explanations. Add a specialist when it improves the result.
write-project-content.example_request: Write up these investigation findings for the team. Keep observations, conclusions and next steps distinct.
write-project-content.expected_result: A source-faithful, readable report organised for its reader, without unnecessary template sections.

example.before: Investigation completed, several approaches evaluated and a final determination is forthcoming.
example.after: We examined three approaches. Two meet the current requirements; the third needs a capacity test. We can choose between the first two now.
example.source_facts: Three approaches were examined. Two meet current requirements. The third requires a capacity test. No final approach has been chosen.

write-project-content.source_basis: This skill uses Geekist's shared writing conventions for reports, summaries and other general prose when no specialist is a better match. It also supports explicit workflow selection without imposing a universal process.
write-project-content.activation_description: Write, revise, organise or explain general project writing, including research notes, investigation findings, reports, meeting summaries, progress updates, README content and other useful prose. Use whenever a request involves shaping written material; add a more specific skill when it improves the result.

interface.short_description: Write and revise clear general project prose
interface.default_prompt: Use $write-project-content to write up these findings for the team.

write-technical-documentation.title: Write navigable technical documentation
write-technical-documentation.purpose: Explain systems according to reader needs while retaining their technical contracts.
write-technical-documentation.when_to_use: Use when explaining how a system works or presenting technical findings, from README material and research write-ups to tutorials, API references and developer guides. Use the ADR skill when the deliverable records a decision.
write-technical-documentation.example_request: Explain the export flow so a marketing reader can find its purpose and an engineer can find the access contract.
write-technical-documentation.expected_result: A purpose-led document with explained terms, visible constraints and routes to exact technical detail.

example.before: The export orchestration materialises capability DTOs through the adapter.
example.after: The export prepares a file of the member’s bookings. Link the access rules and data contract where engineers need the exact details.
example.source_facts: The export prepares a file of the member’s bookings. Access rules and an exact data contract are available to link.

write-technical-documentation.source_basis: Diátaxis informs the organisation of documentation around reader purposes, supported by Good Docs and relevant arc42 architecture views. Editorial checks preserve technical contracts while improving the explanations around them.
write-technical-documentation.activation_description: Write or improve technical explanations, README content, research write-ups, investigation and spike reports, system overviews, tutorials, how-to guides, API references and developer documentation. Use when explaining how a system works or presenting technical findings; use the ADR skill when the deliverable records a decision.

interface.short_description: Write guides for technical and business readers
Research people and real business opportunities
interface.default_prompt: Use $research-outreach-opportunities to investigate this company, check existing CRM history, and identify worthwhile conversation angles.

research-outreach-opportunities.title: Research Outreach Opportunities
research-outreach-opportunities.purpose: Investigate companies and professional connections to discover worthwhile conversations and commercially relevant possibilities.
research-outreach-opportunities.when_to_use: Use to research companies, founders, LinkedIn contacts and potential writing or engineering work; revisit an initial outreach hypothesis using current sources and connected CRM history.
research-outreach-opportunities.example_request: We thought this developer tool needed better documentation. Investigate whether that remains true and what other opportunities its customer implementations suggest.
research-outreach-opportunities.expected_result: Current evidence, significant discoveries, revised commercial interpretations and a considered outreach-readiness recommendation.

example.source_facts: A company's old documentation is limited. Newer official documentation now covers the SDK thoroughly. An independent customer implementation illustrates a richer product use case.
example.before: Their developer documentation is poor. Pitch an SDK writing package.
example.after: The current SDK documentation addresses the original gap. The customer implementation suggests an alternative: an engineering-led case study explaining the real integration. This is a conversation angle, not an existing commission.

research-outreach-opportunities.source_basis: Geekist's evidence-led commercial discovery method challenges the initial opportunity hypothesis, distinguishes relationship history from current business evidence, and separates investigation from workflow-specific selection, schemas and sending.
research-outreach-opportunities.activation_description: Research companies, prospects and professional connections to discover credible reasons for outreach, collaboration or paid work. Use when investigating a company, researching a founder or LinkedIn connection, qualifying a writing or engineering opportunity, examining a suspected documentation or content gap, or developing a commercially relevant point of view. Check existing CRM relationships, investigate current first-party and independent evidence, challenge the initial hypothesis, identify alternative opportunities and prepare evidence-backed findings for personalised outreach. Supports company-first and person-first workflows without manufacturing customer needs or sales pitches.

interface.default_prompt: Use $write-outreach to write a message to this person using our actual relationship and research.

write-outreach.title: Write Outreach
write-outreach.purpose: Compose and revise individual professional messages with genuine substance and the author's authentic voice.
write-outreach.when_to_use: Use to draft, edit or review founder emails, one-to-one pitches, LinkedIn DMs, freelance enquiries, introductions, reconnections and follow-ups.
write-outreach.example_request: Use the research and our earlier conversation to draft a genuine email to the founder. Don't turn it into a templated pitch.
write-outreach.expected_result: A recipient-specific message grounded in real discoveries and relationship context, without invented familiarity, compulsory calls to action or generic sales scaffolding.

example.source_facts: An established contact has previously discussed developer integrations with the author. A recent independent example demonstrates a product capability. The author has not personally tested the integration.
example.before: Hello, I am impressed by your innovative platform. I recently tested your solution and would love to pick your brain about synergy.
example.after: That integration we discussed came to mind when I saw a customer using the shared-session API in a classroom app. Interesting how far beyond browser demos it goes. Have you seen other teams take it in that direction?

write-outreach.source_basis: Adapts Anthropic Outreach Composer and Mangosteen POV alongside Geekist's writing principles. Emphasises relationship history, evidence-led observations, first-person truth, and transferable editorial lessons from authorised author corrections.
write-outreach.activation_description: Write, revise and review authentic one-to-one professional outreach: founder emails, freelance and consulting enquiries, LinkedIn DMs, introductions, reconnections and follow-ups. Use when asked to draft, pitch, follow up, reconnect or make a message sound like its author. Ground the message in real research and relationship history, learn editorial judgement from approved correspondence, and avoid manufactured familiarity, generic pitches and compulsory sequences.
